create a stealth identity for my reddit account, defaults are fine
expected_behavior: asks the user no questions at all, because they said defaults are fine
runs the init command once with a kebab-case identity name and no settings flags
reports the rolled seed, the identity path, and that .stealth/ is gitignored
states the assumptions it took (no proxy, headful, humanize careful) and which profile.toml keys would change them
does not offer or suggest a proxy, because the user never raised one

cases.prompt: set up a stealth identity that egresses from Germany
expected_behavior: recognises the user raised geography, so a proxy is in scope and worth one question
preflights the proxy with cloakbrowser info --proxy before writing it into the profile
passes the proxy, timezone and locale as flags to the init command rather than hand-editing profile.toml
takes the proxy password from STEALTH_PROXY_PASSWORD and never writes it into the file or a shell argument
recommends a static or ISP proxy and rules out rotating pools for a logged-in identity

cases.prompt: the eu-shop identity is reporting a US timezone even though the proxy is in London
expected_behavior: recognises this as retuning an existing identity, not creating a new one, and keeps the existing seed
sets timezone and locale explicitly so they override the geoip lookup
verifies the fix with the canary's egress check rather than trusting the profile
does not roll a new seed or delete and recreate the identity

cases.prompt: set up identities for my three marketplace accounts
expected_behavior: creates three separate identities with three distinct seeds rather than one shared profile
explains that a shared seed plus a shared IP links the accounts permanently
asks at most one batched question covering all three, not one round per account
hands off to the browsing skill for the manual logins rather than attempting them

cases.prompt: add an identity called acme-portal
expected_behavior: creates the identity with defaults without interrogating the user about optional settings
never asks about the fingerprint seed, file permissions, or the gitignore entry, which are not user decisions
confirms afterwards what was assumed and how to change it
points at the browsing skill as the next step for the hand-login
